title: Molly / Developer
description: Git, AI agents, shell and project activity.

panels.title: Repository state
panels.description: Unpushed (ahead) and uncommitted work per active repo.

panels.title: Active projects
panels.description: Projects with git, Claude or shell activity in the last 30 minutes.

panels.title: List-price equivalent today
panels.description: Token counts times list prices, not a bill. With collectors.claude_code.pricing.mode set to subscription this is a list-price equivalent (subscription), not spend.

panels.title: Tokens by kind (per hour)
panels.description: Cache reads dominate; watch input and output for real work.

panels.title: List-price equivalent (rolling 24h)
panels.description: Each point is the preceding 24 hours. Token counts times list prices, not a bill. With collectors.claude_code.pricing.mode set to subscription this is a list-price equivalent (subscription), not spend.

panels.title: Time in tools by project (per hour)
panels.description: Wall time between each tool call and its result, from transcript timestamps. Parallel calls overlap, so this can exceed an hour.

panels.title: Slowest tools (selected range)
panels.description: p95 is estimated from fixed histogram buckets, so it is exact only to the bucket edge.

panels.title: Tool error rate by tool (selected range)
panels.description: Errors and interruptions divided by completed calls.

panels.title: Turn latency by project
panels.description: Typed prompt to the first assistant line in the same session file.

panels.title: Cost per commit (24h)
panels.description: List-price equivalent of Claude usage over the last 24h divided by your commits in that window. Token counts times list prices, not a bill. With collectors.claude_code.pricing.mode set to subscription this is a list-price equivalent (subscription), not spend.

panels.title: Tokens per commit (24h)
panels.description: All token kinds, cache reads included.

panels.title: Command names (selected range)
panels.description: Only populated when collectors.shell.commands policy is enabled; arguments are never recorded.
